title: verification-gap.md misdescribes ci.yml in the same patch: claims CI never compiles the app
evidence:
Separately: no step runs `odin build app` — `app/main.odin` and `app/audio.odin` are compiled by nothing in CI (verified locally that they build today), and no step runs `harness replay` (see the replay finding).
- **Existing test evidence:** read `ci.yml` in full; steps are: build Odin, purity +
  grep gates, `odin test core`, `tools/harness.sh run`, artifact upload on failure.
+      - name: Orchestration-layer tests (driver/snap/bus)
+        run: odin test app/run
+      - name: Game builds (the shipped artifact compiles)
+        run: odin build app -out:"$RUNNER_TEMP/packet-plumber"
detail: The review's claim — 'no step runs odin build app'; CI runs 'only odin test core + tools/harness.sh run' — is false against the ci.yml in the same patch, which builds the app and tests app/run; its CI-gap conclusion is invalid.
recommended_fix: Re-derive the CI finding from the actual ci.yml in this patch: the app-compile gap is already closed by the 'Game builds' step; drop the claim or re-scope it to the missing Windows/arm64 legs and the absent replay invocation.

title: verification-gap.md asserts upgrade_pipe is unparseable and unused by any demo — draw_and_upgrade.dem in the same patch uses it
evidence:
- The parser's own header comment (`harness/demo_parse.odin:71-74`) documents
  `upgrade_pipe <a>-<b> <tier>` — there is no `case "upgrade_pipe"` (unknown-intent
  error). `resolve_names` handles `Cmd_Upgrade_Pipe`/`Cmd_Set_Lane_Weights`
  (`:218-226`) — dead resolution for unparseable commands. Net effect: **the upgrade
  command is reachable only from core unit tests** — no demo, no golden, and no app
  UI either
+at 200ms upgrade_pipe router-house_a wide -> ok
+at 400ms upgrade_pipe host-router narrow -> span_exceeds_tier
detail: The review claims 'no case upgrade_pipe' and 'reachable only from core unit tests — no demo'; this patch adds draw_and_upgrade.dem with two upgrade_pipe intents and expected results. Either the parser gained the case or the new demo cannot parse — both contradict the review.
recommended_fix: Re-check the parser before merging: if upgrade_pipe parses, correct the review and cite draw_and_upgrade.dem as the integration pin (goldens exist for it); if it doesn't parse, the new demo is broken and the harness gate will fail.

title: CI never builds the gitignored software renderer that T2 requires
evidence:
+      - name: Golden harness (T1 hashes + T2 software pixels + replay gate)
+        run: tools/harness.sh run
+tools/raylib-sw/
+T2 — pixel goldens via raylib 6.0's rlsw software renderer +
  PLATFORM_MEMORY (built by `tools/build_raylib_sw.sh`): bit-exact across
  machines, no display.
detail: tools/raylib-sw/ is gitignored, so a fresh CI checkout has no renderer, yet no CI step calls tools/build_raylib_sw.sh before the golden harness step. Either harness.sh must self-build it (undocumented) or T2 fails on every runner.
recommended_fix: Add an explicit tools/build_raylib_sw.sh step (or a documented self-build inside harness.sh) before 'Golden harness', and verify the vendored raylib-sw build works on macos-latest arm64 runners.

title: Compiled game binary app.bin committed at repo root; .gitignore misses it
evidence:
diff --git a/app.bin b/app.bin
new file mode 100755
index 0000000..4aaf130
Binary files /dev/null and b/app.bin differ
+bin/
detail: A 100755 binary artifact ships in the patch while .gitignore only adds bin/. README's own build command (odin build app) produces exactly this file, so every local build dirties the tree and stale platform-specific binaries can land in main.
recommended_fix: Remove app.bin from the tree and add it (or *.bin) to .gitignore alongside bin/; CI already produces its own artifact in RUNNER_TEMP, so the committed binary serves no purpose.

title: edge-case-hunter W1 says E30 hysteresis 'has no catalog fields' — balance.json ships breach_exit_pct and gradual-grace knobs
evidence:
**potential_consequence:** under flapping SLA the grace window never empties, the meter never drains, and a chronically degraded run is practically unlosable; E30's enter/exit-threshold hysteresis has no catalog fields and no implementation at all
+"win_uptime_pct": 90,
+"breach_exit_pct": 93,
+"grace_refill_per_tick": 5,
+"grace_refill_streak_ticks": 50,
detail: W1 claims no catalog fields exist for the enter/exit hysteresis and offers gradual refill as a fix; balance.json in the same patch defines win_uptime_pct/breach_exit_pct (an enter/exit pair) and grace_refill_per_tick/grace_refill_streak_ticks. Either these are more dead knobs (N7-style) or W1 misreads health.odin.
recommended_fix: Verify whether the code reads breach_exit_pct/grace_refill_*; if unread, list them with the rolling_window_ticks dead-knob finding; if read, correct W1's 'no catalog fields' claim.

title: edge-case-hunter E24 premise 'the catalog always demands both' contradicts demand.json (eras 1–2: email only)
detail: demand.json eras 1 and 2 list only email; streaming demand appears only in era 3. If eras are time-gated, a zero-traffic class is the normal early-run state, so the 'always demands both' premise behind E24's latency note is false.
recommended_fix: Reconcile: either state when era 3 starts (and add a zero-traffic-era test — cheap), or amend the review note to acknowledge streaming demand is absent pre-era-3.

title: node_types.json comment: 'run starts with a MID router' but router_mid is era_introduced 3
evidence:
The run starts with a MID router; map growth spawns BASIC routers.
+    { "id": "router_mid",   "display_name": "Mid Router",   "kind": "junction", "terminal_role": "none",         "throughput_units": 60,  "lb_mode_capable": true,  "era_introduced": 3, "port_capacity": 8 },
detail: The bootstrap map starts with a Mid Router and a content_host, yet runs begin in era 1 per demand.json. If era_introduced gates content, the bootstrap violates it; if it only gates growth/purchases, the comment should say so.
recommended_fix: Clarify whether era_introduced applies to bootstrap content; if so, move router_mid/content_host to era 1 or explain the exemption in the catalog comment.

title: palette.json defines 4 house colors; growth can spawn ~17 residential nodes (house_e..house_z)
detail: The palette has exactly 4 house_body/house_roof colors, while growth_pool_size 24 with the 7-role list repeats ~3.4x, yielding well over a dozen residential spawns named house_e..house_z. The renderer must cycle or clamp; nothing in the data documents which.
recommended_fix: Add a documented cycling rule (idx mod len) or extend house_bodies/house_roofs to cover growth_pool_size; a test asserting every spawn index resolves in-range would pin it.

title: README pins 'dev-2026-08' but .odin-version holds dev-2026-08-nightly — a moving tag, not a pin
evidence:
+dev-2026-08-nightly
+**Engine:** Odin (`dev-2026-08` pin) + raylib 6.0 (`vendor:raylib`). The
+# Odin has no apt/brew pin channel for exact nightly pins; build the
+      # pinned toolchain from source (the .odin-version pin moves only
+      # deliberately — see project-context.md).
+          git clone --depth 1 --branch "$PIN" https://github.com/odin-lang/Odin.git "$RUNNER_TEMP/odin-src"
detail: README and the pin file name different refs, and a '-nightly' tag moves by definition — CI's 'pinned toolchain' (git clone --branch dev-2026-08-nightly) can change compiler behavior between runs without any deliberate move, undermining the determinism claim.
recommended_fix: Point .odin-version at an immutable release/commit (or record the resolved SHA in CI), and align README's pin label with the file's actual value.

title: CI step labeled 'replay gate' runs only tools/harness.sh run — no replay invocation exists in CI
evidence:
+      - name: Golden harness (T1 hashes + T2 software pixels + replay gate)
+        run: tools/harness.sh run
+  `ci.yml` runs only `odin test core` +
+  `tools/harness.sh run`; `replay` appears in no CI step and no script default.
detail: The step name promises a 'replay gate', but the command is tools/harness.sh run, and the same patch's review says replay appears in no CI step and no script default. The label overclaims unless harness.sh run internally replays.
recommended_fix: Either invoke harness replay per demo in CI, or rename the step to drop the 'replay gate' claim; document whether harness.sh run performs the log round-trip check internally.

title: The two review docs cite frames_per_tick at different lines: main.odin:169 (W2) vs main.odin:136 (verification-gap)
evidence:
- **location:** harness/main.odin:169 (`frames_per_tick := FRAME_HZ / int(catalogs.balance.logic_hz)`) + harness/main.odin:203 (`frame % i64(frames_per_tick)`)
+- **Changed surface:** `harness/main.odin:136` (`frames_per_tick := 60 / logic_hz`,
  integer division) vs the loader rule (`core/catalog.odin:317-320`).
detail: Both reviews describe the same expression, one at :169/:203 and the other at :136. Same-revision review docs should agree; a wrong line number sends the fix to the wrong place.
recommended_fix: Pick one canonical citation (re-verify against the merged tree) and reuse it in both docs; add a lint that spot-checks cited line numbers.
